title: Chanan the Wicked
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Rav Huna’s time, as in [Bava Kamma 37a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.37a.3): he struck a certain man; the case came before Rav Huna, who said to Chanan, “Go, give him half a zuz.” He had a bad zuz that he could not exchange; he struck him again and gave him the whole zuz. There, [at 115a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.115a.14-16), he stole a cloak and sold it; [the case] came before Rav Huna, and they said there: “Granted that he is notorious for wickedness, he is not notorious for theft.”[^1]

notes.text: At 37a Rav Huna orders the half-zuz payment. At 115a the Gemara distinguishes a reputation for wickedness from a reputation for theft.
